did_you_know.text: Did you know? This verse describes an unusual situation in which seven women ask to be called by one man’s name, declaring that they will provide their own food and clothing. Their only request is to have their disgrace removed through a marriage relationship.

Did you know? The expression “the Branch of the LORD” appears in the verse as a symbol of beauty and honor, alongside “the fruit of the land,” which is described as the pride and glory of Israel’s survivors.
Did you know? This is the first verse in the chapter to introduce the idea of “Israel’s survivors”—a remnant that will be spared and associated with blessing and honor.
Did you know? The remnant remaining in Zion and Jerusalem will be called holy, and the verse connects them with “all who are recorded among the living in Jerusalem.”

Did you know? Jerusalem’s cleansing is described as taking place through two means: “a spirit of judgment” and “a spirit of burning.” According to the verse, this cleansing removes the filth of the daughters of Zion and the bloodstains of Jerusalem.

Did you know? The chapter’s description of God’s presence includes a cloud and smoke by day and the light of a blazing fire by night, over every part of Mount Zion and over its assemblies—the places where people gather.
Did you know? The word “canopy” in this verse describes divine covering over all the glory. Thus, the canopy is both an image of glory and of protective presence.
Did you know? The divine covering is also described as a practical shelter: a booth providing shade from the heat of day and refuge from wind, storm, and rain.
